In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MSP2 and MSP-3 proteins of A. marginale are immunogenic and are able to induce a T-lymphocytic response in vaccinated animals.
the CD4+ T cell response is directed to conserved epitopes in the N termini and the C termini of the MSP2 and MSP 3 proteins.
MSP2 and MSP2-specific CD4+ T cell epitopes are conserved in MSP2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD4+ T cell response to MSP3 and MSP2 in A. marginale-immune animals may be directed against conserved and partially-conserved epitopes in the N and/or C termini of these proteins.
CD4+ cells recognize epitopes conserved between MSP2 and MSP-3.
MSP2 and MSP2-specific CD4+ T-lymphocytes are important to the immune response to the vaccine and to the immune response of cattle that have recovered from infection with A. marginale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conserved regions of MSP3 are processed and presented by APCs to T cells.
MSP2 and MSP2-like proteins are important targets for CD4+ T cell recognition in the immune response to A. marginale.
